ideas: What became more expensive and when
How you changed your spending because of it

phrases.meaning: money needed for basic daily needs
have just enough money to live

model: A price increase that really affected me was when my rent went up last year. I rent a small studio flat in Da Nang, and in January my landlord told me it would go up in price by about fifteen percent. She explained that it was due to higher electricity bills and the fact that the area had become more popular with tourists, which means that owners can now charge more. I understood her reasons, but it was still a shock, because my salary hadn't changed at all. As a consequence, I really started to feel the pinch. On top of that, rising fuel prices meant that riding to work cost more too, and even my favourite café passed the cost on to customers by raising its prices. So the cost of living suddenly felt much higher. I didn't have any problem making ends meet, but I had to be much more careful. I started to look for cheaper options for almost everything. For example, I switched to a cheaper phone plan and began buying vegetables at the local market instead of the supermarket. I also looked at other flats, but anything closer to the city centre was out of my budget. In the end I stayed, and actually, the experience led to me making a proper monthly budget for the first time. So although it was stressful, it made me better with money.
